ownerAndVersionChecks.scope: Production client and personal library HTTP handler with an in-memory Firestore transaction fixture.
observed: First join added one library preferences record; a second identical HTTP request changed no stored data.
The other account retained its separate selection. A later public edition became available to the follower.
Repeated join preserved an imported older fixed version, its disabled state, and its revision.
The handler rejected stale version IDs on first join and rejected a withdrawn source.

agent.scope: Formal Firestore Agent assembly, ADK Runner, encrypted result storage in a transaction fixture and frontend result projection. The provider and catalogue were scripted.

earlierAttempts: The initial HTTP regression returned 400 for an unknown join shape; after implementation a stale edition returned 409.
The new chat tools were initially absent. The completed run returned the server receipt and a link to the series.
The sandbox could not start the emulator hub. The isolated runner started with sandbox approval.
Firebase Auth's local emulator banner intercepted the pointer on the chat footer. The same accessible link opened with Enter.
The browser traffic assertion initially counted POST care/search as a write. The next run classified that exact read endpoint separately and still required a single library mutation.
